title: Customs Tariff Amendment (Carbon Tax Repeal) Bill 2013
short_title: Customs Tariff Amendment (Carbon Tax Repeal) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill is part of a package that repeals the carbon tax and includes measures to prevent price exploitation.

The package would prohibit businesses from engaging in carbon-specific price exploitation for key goods like electricity and gas, with penalties of up to 6,471 penalty units for corporations and 1,295 for individuals.
The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission would gain monitoring powers to assess the effect of the repeal on prices and assist in enforcing the new prohibition.
changes: Introduces a new prohibition on carbon-specific price exploitation for key goods.
Gives the ACCC powers to monitor prices and assess the effect of the carbon tax repeal.
Prohibits false or misleading representations about the carbon tax repeal's effect on prices.
summary.affected: Businesses supplying key goods such as electricity and gas, and consumers.

speeches.speaker: Joe Hockey
speeches.brief: Moved that the bill be read a second time, proposing changes to remove carbon tax elements from customs duties on aviation fuel and reduce airline costs, including surcharges of between $1.93 and $7.25 per passenger.

speeches.speaker: Christopher Pyne
speeches.brief: Moved a debate management motion to conclude debate on the Clean Energy Legislation (Carbon Tax Repeal) Bill 2013 and related bills by Thursday this week, arguing the election gave the coalition a mandate with 90 seats to Labor's 55, Labor's worst result since 1903.

speeches.speaker: Bill Shorten
speeches.brief: Argued against the government's carbon tax repeal bills, saying the decade from 2001 to 2010 was the warmest on record, that Direct Action would cost households an estimated $1,200 a year without a legislated cap on emissions, and noted that under Labor wind power generation trebled and 24,000 renewable energy jobs were created.

speeches.speaker: Mitch Fifield
speeches.brief: The speaker moved the Customs Tariff Amendment (Carbon Tax Repeal) Bill 2013 to remove carbon tax elements from the Customs Tariff Act, arguing it would reduce excise-equivalent customs duty on aviation fuel and citing Qantas surcharges of $1.93–$7.25 per passenger and similar Virgin Australia surcharges, with the repeal expected to lower airline costs and enable savings for travellers.

speeches.speaker: Christopher Pyne
speeches.brief: Answered that the carbon tax cost Qantas $106 million and Virgin $45 million last financial year, and said carbon tax repeal bills already before the Senate could be passed immediately with opposition support to help airline jobs, accusing the Leader of the Opposition of favouring Qantas unions over workers.
